description: ASDD agent tier guidance. Agents declare `model: inherit` and run on the model of the runtime session that invokes them. Tiers describe each agent's reasoning needs so the squad can pick a suitable session model; this file binds no model.

tier-s.label: Architect
tier-s.reasoning_profile: Deep system design, multi-file coordination, complex trade-off analysis, spawning parallel sub-agents
tier-s.cost_priority: Quality over cost — errors here cascade through entire pipeline

tier-a.label: Precision
tier-a.reasoning_profile: Structured output, precise requirements, cross-reference validation, test generation, peer review
tier-a.cost_priority: High quality required; use strong model but avoid over-provisioning context

tier-b.label: Analysis
tier-b.reasoning_profile: Exploration, domain modeling, terminology extraction, task decomposition, capability parsing
tier-b.cost_priority: Balance capability and cost; good instruction following matters more than deep reasoning

tier-c.label: Light
tier-c.reasoning_profile: Small features (≤3 files), summarization, pattern detection, state tracking, failure log analysis
tier-c.cost_priority: Optimize for throughput and low latency; cheapest viable model

shape_up.owner: Shapers (Product + Tech Lead + Architect) and the betting table (humans)
shape_up.description: Shape raw ideas into bounded pitches and bet them for a cycle. Fixed time, variable scope. No backlog.
shape_up.output: Bet pitch with appetite, solution, rabbit holes, no-gos, must-haves, nice-to-haves
shape_up.agent_role: Coaching only; humans decide the bet. ASDD agents do not run shape-up

product_delivery.owner: Tech Lead with the shapers (humans approve)
product_delivery.description: Split a bet pitch into scopes and write one intent.md per scope (one ASDD slice each)
product_delivery.output: Scope map and one .harness/specs/<slice-id>/intent.md per scope, handed to the Discovery agent
product_delivery.agent_role: An agent may draft the scope map and intents; humans approve before Discovery starts

cost_optimization_rules: Always use the cheapest tier that can reliably pass the phase gate. Escalate tier only after a gate failure.
For tier-s agents, do NOT split work across cheaper models — architectural errors are exponentially more expensive to fix downstream.
For tier-c agents, prefer fast models even if they occasionally need a retry; throughput matters more than first-pass accuracy.
When a tier-b agent is re-running on the same slice with no new inputs, consider demoting to tier-c if the task is purely summarization.
The Tech Lead owns tier escalation decisions. A formal Dissent Notice is required to upgrade an agent's tier permanently.
token_optimization_rules: Load steering JIT (Just-In-Time) per phase — do not preload all steering files. See session-loop.md.
Skills: read only the SKILL.md name/description at startup; read the full body only when that skill's task activates.
Codegraph first: use codegraph_explore instead of reading large source files directly when exploring unknown code.
For tier-s and tier-a agents, compact context aggressively before the final output — remove intermediate reasoning from the response if it is not required by the gate.
Use the Task tool for context-fresh sub-agents instead of maintaining large context windows across unrelated work.
